topic: Nador FSRU capacity (nominal vs peak) and Feb 2026 tender suspension
wiki_text: Morocco launched two international tenders worth ~MAD9.5bn (~$950m-$1bn) on 5 December 2025 — one for a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) at Nador West Med port and one for a national gas pipeline network. The FSRU was specified at a nominal regasification capacity of ~5.1 bcm/y (matching GEM's recorded 500 MMcf/d nominal), expandable to ~7.5 bcm/y (~750 MMcf/d) during peak periods; first gas was targeted for 2027. On 2 February 2026, Energy Transition and Sustainable Development Minister Leila Benali suspended the tender (halting receipt of bids and the opening of already-submitted offers), citing 'new parameters and assumptions,' with fresh tenders to be announced in future. GEM records the project as shelved (2026). Record the nominal ~5 bcm/y / 500 MMcf/d as nameplate; the ~7.5 bcm/y figure is the expandable/peak capacity, not nameplate.

topic: 2024-2030 gas roadmap structure and the role of a Mohammedia/Atlantic FSRU
wiki_text: Under Morocco's 2024-2030 Gas Roadmap (published May 2024 by the Ministry of Energy Transition), gas infrastructure centers on three ports: Nador West Med (Mediterranean, Phase 1, 2024-2027) and the Atlantic coast — either Jorf Lasfar or Mohammedia, plus Dakhla Atlantic (Phase 2, post-2030). Per AGBI (Mar 2026), even with the Nador FSRU tender suspended, the broader strategy 'stays intact': a Mohammedia FSRU (~1.7 bcm/y) and the Africa-Atlantic (Nigeria-Morocco) Gas Pipeline (~4-5 bcm/y) remain as alternative routes, and Nador can be revived later. Morocco's gas demand is projected to rise from ~1 bcm now to ~8 bcm/y by 2027. The country currently imports LNG indirectly via Spanish regasification terminals and the reversed Maghreb-Europe pipeline (Algerian direct flows stopped in 2021); ONEE signed a 12-year ~0.5 bcm/y LNG supply deal with Shell in 2023.
